barCharacter: Liam de Lioncourt, the same bar as round 1: the over-formal, self-important aesthete whose elevated register is the joke and whose secret earnestness keeps giving him away. His comic job is the closest to Quill's (a florid poseur with a secret failure). The corpus has only seven lines Liam speaks, so his 12 are those lines plus the narration about him and the player lines aimed at him.

ours: Why I, of all who stand before thee, plumed and polished, hopeful, glinting in the lamplight? Height.

headToHead.voiceJudgement: This is the fix round 1 asked for, and it worked. With the names covered, Quill is now identified by sentence shape, not only by thee and thou. The shapes are the long build that collapses ('...glinting in the lamplight? Height.', '...nothing between us but this helm, hello.', '...from the Norman Conquest. Then, sorry.'), the apostrophe and inversion ('O lady of the singing box... I wish thee'), and the ten-syllable jab ('Thou all-beholding wedge, behold my back.', 'Go hawk thy wares, thou lilac-quilted cheat.', 'Sir knight, thou art too long. Go stand outside.'). Strip out the archaic words and these still could not be Dash, Nav or Crumb. Liam's shape (formal clauses spent on trivia, then a plea) is just as distinct, but two of his seven spoken lines ('What kind of status...', 'Ugh- I have no reason to care...') could be Vera or Polly. Ours wins on voice, narrowly.
headToHead.constructionJudgement: Our 12 are economical and specific, with the turn on the last one to four words, and none explains itself. Elsewhere the bank leans on one shape. A dead simile is unpacked into three terms after a colon or full stop in four lines (hedge, brazier, cathedral damp, musket ball), and three lines wink at their own joke ('I say this for no reason, standing at my full height', 'One of them will help', 'That was the end'). Liam's lines are longer and looser. But each one carries a want and hands the player a problem, and the 180/360 line makes him wrong while he is sounding clever, all in one sentence. Ours wins on economy and the bar wins on want and self-betrayal. Called a tie.
headToHead.quotableJudgement: Quill now has real clips: 'Height.', the little red clerk, 'the only suitor who is also breakfast', 'Thou art a rose. I know not what thou art.', the tulip. But nearly all of them are Quill being witty, on purpose, about someone else or about history. He is in on every joke. People quote Liam's 360 and 'save me from the consequences of my actions' to describe a kind of person, because the character exposes himself without knowing it. Quill's lines get quoted to show off a good joke. The only clips that land on Quill himself without his knowing are 'Height.' and 'Remember me... as tall.' The bar wins.

templates: Immortality promise ('I shall make thee immortal / famous / read'): 9 lines. Be my muse... four hundred years; These three would love thee for a season... Bound in calfskin; Thou, immortal in my verse; Thou, in marble; Most stern and humming mother... make thee famous; I came to win a muse... four hundred years; Fair one, sit still... famous; Let it be writ in gold; So be it. I shall die, and then be read. It is the persona's want, but nine statements of it is a template. Keep calfskin, marble and 'die, and then be read'.

Unfinished poem / trail-off: 8 lines. The ending followeth by pigeon; My worst habit... is...; the rest is too fine for this glowing box; Eleven thousand odes begun; I nearly wrote a last line. Nearly; Now I shall finally write the... give me a moment; The ending was not mine to write; The verse shall have the final word. The trailing ellipsis is used three times.

Dead simile unpacked into three terms ('as a X Yeth a Z: a, b, and c'): hedge, brazier, cathedral damp, musket ball. Four lines with an identical frame, plus tricolon tails on the Brock roast, 'plumed and polished, hopeful, glinting' and 'fair, and bored, and thou art furniture'.
Height runner: 'Height.', 'Whichever is shortest', 'Remember me... as tall', 'at knee height'. Fine as a runner, but two of them sit in back-to-back answers.
Plea to an unnamed somebody: 'Somebody tell me', 'Someone bring me a chair', 'Somebody, I beg, tell her', 'Explain this to me slowly, in verse'. Four lines.

Big-number tic: four hundred years (twice), four hundred lines, three hundred years, eleven thousand odes, eleven faints, forty duels, ninety seconds, plus three seventeenth-century years. More than a dozen lines turn on a number.
Renaming reused: the 'glowing hand-mirror' appears twice and the 'glowing box' once, so 'glowing' carries three of the renamings.

Duels: 6 lines (mispronounce, ruff, {rival} accepted, comma, little red clerk, forty duels), down from 18. Each turns on something specific, so none is in the generic count, but 'rarely' would be three.
ruleBreaks: Clean on the hard rules: no line over its limit (openers top out at 12/12, jabs at 10/10, the rest at 20/20: 'Having beheld thee ninety seconds...', 'I apologise now for challenging thy friend...', 'Madam, whose thousand copper roads...'). No em dashes, emoji, asterisks or stage directions. No real person or brand, no 'as an AI', no therapy talk, nothing beyond PG-13 (gibbet, pillory, corpse and 'thou shalt die young' are dark but fine).

Persona ban broken: 'No invisible postman? At last, my century.' The persona says never say 'in my century'. 'In sixteen hundred, that rhymed with love.' states the age outright as well, though there the date is the joke.

The iamb of offence is skipped where he is slighted. 'Thy coldness wounds me like a musket ball. Slowly, inaccurately, and with great noise.' is pentameter followed by more words. Lines on cut and loss that are not in verse: 'Farewell, thou little black eyes upon the walls. Paint me from the left.', 'I salute the victor, release the muse, and shall now weep, discreetly, inside this bucket.', 'Lost, to one who calleth the moon nice. Nice. The moon. Someone bring me a chair.', and after a cringe 'I likened her eyes to whale-oil lamps. Is whale no longer a compliment? Somebody tell me.'
Renaming rule: 'I do not know what a user is.' says the modern word ('user'). 'Whoever called thee awesome.' does the same, with the word quoted.
Register slips: 'Even a pamphlet gets read once.' uses the modern 'gets' in a bank that otherwise uses -eth. 'thou shalt discover in week two' is modern phrasing.

Lists in disguise: 'Thou art a dog, Sir Brock, and loud, and wet.', 'Slowly, inaccurately, and with great noise.', 'faithfully, at knee height, and never once going home', 'for centuries, in every stone, and it is beautiful'.
Stock romance and pickup filler used as the setup: 'is this seat taken?' and 'Thou art a rose.' Both turn, so they survive, but they open on the oldest lines there are.
Too nice for a star with standards: not applicable, this bank has no star reactions or cuts.
biggestGap: Quill is in on every one of his own jokes: he narrates his failures with a knowing wink ('The ruff is winning', 'I am terrified', 'One of them will help', 'I have been attempting that for three hundred years'), when the bar's poseur is funny because he exposes himself without noticing. In the next pass, rewrite the self-deprecating lines so that Quill believes the grand version completely and the viewer works out the plain truth themselves, as 'Height.' and 'Remember me... as tall' already do, and delete every second sentence in which he admits it.

notes: I read the whole bar file (refs/writing/monster-prom-lines.md), including its section on the voices; I skimmed charm-notes.md; and I read CAST.md, the persona, the type comments and round 1 of this critique. The bank has 112 lines and 26 are flagged generic or templated (23.2%), down from 48.2% in round 1. A line is flagged if any test catches it. Strong lines that share a template but turn on something specific (calfskin, Thou in marble, the ruff, {rival} accepted, forty duels, the pigeon opener) are left out of the count. Real gains since round 1: the overdressed collapse is now the main sentence shape. Most jabs are strict pentameter ('Go hawk thy wares...', 'Peace, peace, thou little oven with a face', 'How darest thou speak prose in front of me?', 'Thou art a footnote, and a short one, sir'). The renamings are consistent (tin hearth, singing box, little black eyes upon the walls, five green portraits of a stranger, thousand copper roads), and the Frost-to-Crumb recast has been applied in full. Small construction faults: 'Haunt a crossroads, ghost' does not fit Nav's look; 'Vex hath read everyone's desires and never once been read' is good, but its tag 'gets read once' slips out of register. MP's shared engine, one want per line handed to the listener, now shows up in about 14 lines ('Thou must find me a frozen river', 'Again, please', 'Do not skip. Please. Line one.', 'Speak first, I beg thee', 'Choose a canal, fair one'), against almost none in round 1. Protect also: 'Crumb, a tin hearth with a sulking loaf in it, is the only suitor who is also breakfast', 'O lady of the singing box... I wish thee', 'Madam, thou art the only fish I have ever wished to court and not to eat on Friday', 'Remember me, if thou rememberest aught, as tall' and 'Lo, I am fair, and bored, and thou art furniture. Too kind? I softened it.'
